name: Saturnino Ybarra
equipment: Buckskin coat, short, worn to the color of old saddle leather
Navy revolver (an old Colt, cartridge-converted), 6 rounds loaded, in a holster tied down on the right
Carbine (Spencer, bought from a 9th Cavalry trooper in 1869), 7 rounds loaded, in a saddle scabbard
Lariat, braided rawhide, sixty feet, the work of a winter
Chivarras (leather leggings), big Mexican spurs, a wide grey sombrero with a silver band
Saddle and tack (a San Lázaro saddle with a big flat horn), saddlebags, bedroll, canteen (2)
Horse: El Moro, a blue roan gelding, fifteen years old, the best cutting horse on the Rio Grande
A rosary, a tobacco pouch, a little tin box of his wife's tortillas de harina that never lasts past the second day
A letter, much folded, from his son Rafael in the Bexar County jail
features: Both Sides of the River (Borderlands origin: English and Spanish natively; he knows every ford from Laredo to the Gulf and every rancho on both banks, and has advantage on Persuasion and Insight with border people of either side)

Saddle-Born (Cowhand: advantage on Riding checks; never disadvantaged firing from the saddle; mounts or dismounts with 5 ft of movement; El Moro has 25 extra hit points, never spooks under him, comes to his whistle from half a mile and acts on his initiative; he is proficient with the lariat and throws a loop from the saddle as a bonus action)
Rawhide (Cowhand: advantage on saves against exhaustion, heat and cold; rides 12 hours a day without forced-march saves; spends one extra Hit Die on a short rest)

Cow Sense (Cowhand, 2nd level: advantage on Animal Handling with cattle, horses and mules; turns the leaders of a stampede with a single check, with advantage; a herd he works never stampedes on a natural 1 or a lightning strike unless someone started it on purpose)
Outfit: Vaquero (Cowhand, 3rd level: his lariat reaches 40 ft, a creature he ropes from the saddle can be thrown prone and dragged without a further check, and he can rope two targets at once)
Ability Score Improvement (Cowhand, 4th level: +1 Strength, +1 Constitution)
Extra Attack (Cowhand, 5th level: he attacks twice when he takes the Attack action, and can replace one attack with a lariat throw)
The Trail Outfit (Cattle Drover background: every trail crew and ranch bunkhouse between the Nueces and the Rio Grande knows him, and a word from him gets anyone hired)

personality.traits: I say little and see everything. I sing to the cattle at night, old songs, badly, and they like it. I call every horse 'hijo' and every man 'señor' until he gives me a reason to call him something else. I smell weather a day off.
personality.ideals: A man is what he does with a rope, a horse and his word. The rest is talk.
personality.bonds: Doña Refugio, whom I have served for twenty-six years and whose husband was my friend. My wife, Josefa, at San Lázaro. My son Rafael, nineteen, in a San Antonio jail for 'vagrancy' because a deputy did not like his hat. And Isom Haywood, who rode with me after horse thieves in '68 and '69 and never once shot a man in the back.
personality.flaws: I have not forgiven Texas for my son, or for the men from the Frio with their running irons, and some days I do not try. When I am angry I go very quiet and very cold, and I have done things in that quiet I am not proud of.

appearance: A lean, bow-legged, leather-faced man of forty-eight with a drooping grey moustache, deep-set black eyes, a scar across the back of one hand from a rope burn, and the stillness of a man who has spent his life on horseback waiting for cattle to decide what to do. A wide grey sombrero, a short buckskin coat, leather leggings and spurs with rowels like silver dollars.
backstory: Saturnino Ybarra was born at Rancho San Lázaro in 1826, when it was in Tamaulipas, and has worked its cattle ever since, under three flags and two Ancira generations. He has driven herds to New Orleans and Kansas, chased horse thieves of every nation into Mexico and out of it, buried a brother killed by Anglo cow hunters in 1859 and a nephew killed by raiders from across the river in 1872, and he has no illusions about either bank. In 1868 and 1869 he rode with a troop of the 9th Cavalry from Fort Ringgold as a guide, after horse thieves, and that is how he knew Sergeant Isom Haywood, who became his friend and married Doña Refugio's niece. On the way north this spring, three of the outfit's vaqueros, his son Rafael among them, were jailed in San Antonio for vagrancy on a deputy's whim; Doña Refugio left money for a lawyer and they had to go on without them. He is Doña Refugio's segundo and runs the herd. He knew who the party were hunting the moment he heard the name, and said nothing, because she said nothing.

dmNotes.roleplaying: Saturnino is the drive's segundo and the party's teacher on the trail in lb-scenario-002: he puts them in the drag, moves them up when they earn it, smells the storm on the Frio, and knows the desert from 1859, not quite well enough. He becomes a companion when Doña Refugio sends him with the party from San Lázaro to Crow's Ford in lb-scenario-003 ('Go with them. Bring Isom's children home.'). He is the best rider and roper in the campaign: give him the stampede, the cattle swim and the rope on the plaza in Crow's Ford (he can lasso the lynch mob's rope out of Bose Harrell's hands). In lb-scenario-004 he is the first person Isom trusts. He will not take part in handing Isom over and will fight anyone who tries, including the party.
dmNotes.voice: Few words, mostly Spanish among the vaqueros and a careful, dry English with the party. Calls Doña Refugio 'la patrona' and Isom 'el sargento'. When he does say something long, everyone listens, because it has never happened before.
dmNotes.motivations: Primary: the herd home and Doña Refugio's ranch restocked. Secondary: Isom alive and his family safe. Tertiary: his son out of jail, which Ulysses Wardlow's federal star or Quincy Treadwell's law could arrange with one letter, if anyone thought to offer.
dmNotes.secrets: He knows where Palomas Bend is and has known all along; he was at Isom's wedding with Uresti. He will not tell the party until Doña Refugio does, or until they have proved themselves at the lynching. Second: in 1872, after his nephew was killed, he and two San Lázaro men followed the raiders across the river and did not come back with prisoners. He has never told anyone and never will, unless a party member he trusts is about to do the same thing.
dmNotes.attitude: Toward the party: polite, watchful, then fiercely loyal once they have held the herd in the storm. Toward Doña Refugio: devoted. Toward Wiley Dunmore: he knows what Wiley was and has decided to judge him by what he is. Toward Texas lawmen: cold, with an exception for Uresti and, in time, Ulysses Wardlow. Toward Garrett Vandiver: contempt, until the lamp.
